newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Ford says unaffected by Halewood move.
newsitem.headline: German Ford says unaffected by Halewood move.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's decision on Thursday to cut 1,300 jobs at its plant in Halewood, north-west England, has no direct impact on its German plant, a spokeswoman for the German unit said.
"There is no direct impact from this on us," the Ford-Werke AG spokeswoman said in response to enquiries.
Earlier, there had been speculation that Ford in Germany could benefit from a transfer of production from Halewood.

In particular, the spokeswoman ruled out the suggestion that the move would mean that its plant in Saarlouis, in the south-western region of Saarland, would see production of the planned new Escort model switched to it.
She added that the Halewood decision should be seen more in the context of Ford's continued over-capacity in Europe as a whole rather than in any purely national terms.
No such redundancy programme was however planned for the Saarlouis plant, which employs around 6,000 people, she added.

A Ford statement released in Britain earlier held out the possibility that Halewood could still be the European source for a planned new vehicle, subject to performance- and investment-related conditions being met.
